question: Which engine powers the Cessna 152, and what is its rated horsepower and speed?

options.text: Lycoming O-235-L2C, 110 BHP at 2550 RPM
Continental O-200, 100 BHP at 2750 RPM
Lycoming O-320, 160 BHP at 2700 RPM
Lycoming O-235-L2C, 125 BHP at 2700 RPM

explanation: The airplane is powered by a Lycoming Model O-235-L2C rated at 110 horsepower at 2550 RPM.

question: How is the O-235-L2C engine best described in terms of configuration and induction?

options.text: Turbocharged, geared, liquid-cooled, inline, fuel-injected, six-cylinder
Normally-aspirated, direct-drive, air-cooled, horizontally opposed, carburetor-equipped, four-cylinder
Normally-aspirated, geared, air-cooled, radial, carburetor-equipped, four-cylinder
Turbocharged, direct-drive, liquid-cooled, horizontally opposed, fuel-injected, four-cylinder

explanation: The engine is a normally-aspirated, direct-drive, air-cooled, horizontally opposed, carburetor-equipped, four-cylinder engine with 233.3 cubic inch displacement.

question: What is the displacement of the O-235-L2C engine?

options.text: 360 cubic inches
200 cubic inches
233.3 cubic inches
320 cubic inches

explanation: The engine has a displacement of 233.3 cubic inches.

question: What major engine accessories are mounted on the front of the engine?

options.text: Dual magnetos and a vacuum pump
A turbocharger and an intercooler
A propeller governor and a feathering pump
A starter, a belt-driven alternator, and an oil cooler

explanation: Major engine accessories mounted on the front of the engine include a starter, a belt-driven alternator, and an oil cooler; dual magnetos are mounted on the rear accessory drive pad instead.

question: Where are the dual magnetos mounted on the engine?

options.text: On an accessory drive pad on the rear of the engine
On the front of the engine, beside the starter
Inside the oil sump
On the propeller hub

explanation: Dual magnetos are mounted on an accessory drive pad on the rear of the engine.

question: How is the mixture control operated for small versus rapid or large adjustments?

options.text: All adjustments require depressing the lock button
Small adjustments by rotating the knob; rapid/large adjustments by depressing the lock button and repositioning
The mixture control has only two positions: rich and idle cut-off
Small adjustments require the lock button; large ones do not

explanation: For small adjustments the mixture knob is rotated; for rapid or large adjustments, the lock button in the end of the knob is depressed and the control is repositioned directly.

question: What three instruments monitor engine operation?

options.text: Oil pressure gage, cylinder head temperature gage, and manifold pressure gage
Tachometer, fuel flow gage, and EGT gage
Oil pressure gage, oil temperature gage, and tachometer
Oil temperature gage, suction gage, and ammeter

explanation: Engine operation is monitored by the oil pressure gage, oil temperature gage, and tachometer.

question: What type of temperature sensor operates the oil temperature gage, and what powers it?

options.text: A capillary bulb connected directly to the gage, needing no electrical power
A vacuum-operated sensor
A mechanical bimetallic strip, needing no electrical power
An electrical-resistance type sensor, powered by the airplane electrical system

explanation: The oil temperature gage is operated by an electrical-resistance type temperature sensor which receives power from the airplane electrical system.

question: The engine-driven mechanical tachometer indicates both engine and propeller speed, and what else does its hour meter record?

options.text: Elapsed engine time in hours and tenths
Total fuel consumed since the last refueling
Cumulative flight cycles
Time since the last magneto inspection

explanation: An hour meter below the center of the tachometer dial records elapsed engine time in hours and tenths.

question: To ensure proper seating of the rings, how long should a new or overhauled engine be operated at 65-75% power?

options.text: For the first 10 hours only
Until a total of 50 hours has accumulated or oil consumption has stabilized
For exactly 25 hours
There is no recommended break-in period; full power may be used immediately

explanation: It is suggested that cruising be accomplished at 65% to 75% power until a total of 50 hours has accumulated or oil consumption has stabilized, to ensure proper seating of the rings.

question: What kind of oil is the airplane delivered with from the factory, and what should be done with it?

options.text: Dispersant oil, which should never be changed
Straight mineral oil, changed every 10 hours
Corrosion preventive oil, which should be drained after the first 25 hours
Synthetic oil, changed at 100 hours

explanation: The airplane is delivered from the factory with a corrosion preventive aircraft engine oil, which should be drained after the first 25 hours of operation.

question: In the engine oil system, what does the bypass valve do when the oil is cold?

options.text: It routes all oil through the oil cooler before pressure screening
It shuts off oil flow entirely until oil temperature rises
It diverts oil to the vacuum pump
It allows the oil to bypass the oil cooler and go directly to the pressure screen

explanation: If the oil is cold, the bypass valve allows the oil to bypass the oil cooler and go directly from the pump to the oil pressure screen.

question: Where is the oil cooler located?

options.text: On the front side of the left forward engine baffle
Inside the oil sump
Behind the firewall
On top of the propeller spinner

explanation: If the oil is hot, the bypass valve routes it through a flexible hose to the oil cooler on the front side of the left forward engine baffle.

question: Which spark plugs does the right magneto fire, and which does the left magneto fire?

options.text: Right magneto fires all four upper plugs; left magneto fires all four lower plugs
Right magneto fires lower right and upper left; left magneto fires lower left and upper right
Right magneto fires only the right-side cylinders; left magneto fires only the left-side cylinders
Each magneto fires only one spark plug total

explanation: The right magneto fires the lower right and upper left spark plugs; the left magneto fires the lower left and upper right spark plugs.

question: What are the five positions of the ignition-starter rotary switch, in clockwise order?

options.text: OFF, L, R, BOTH, START
OFF, BOTH, L, R, START
OFF, R, L, BOTH, START
START, BOTH, L, R, OFF

explanation: The ignition switch is labeled clockwise: OFF, R, L, BOTH, and START.

question: Why is normal operation conducted with both magnetos (the BOTH position) rather than a single magneto?

options.text: It doubles engine RPM output
It reduces oil consumption
Single-magneto operation is prohibited by the starter interlock
Dual ignition provides more complete burning of the fuel-air mixture

explanation: Normal operation is conducted with both magnetos due to the more complete burning of the fuel-air mixture with dual ignition; the R and L positions are for checking and emergency use only.

question: What removes dust and foreign matter from the air entering the engine's air induction system?

options.text: An air filter covering the intake in the lower cowling
A centrifugal separator ahead of the carburetor
The oil cooler acts as the filter
No filter is fitted; air enters directly from the intake

explanation: The intake in the lower portion of the engine cowling is covered by an air filter which removes dust and other foreign matter from the induction air.

question: Approximately how much RPM loss results from using full carburetor heat at full throttle?

options.text: 10 to 20 RPM
150 to 200 RPM
500 to 600 RPM
There is no RPM loss with carburetor heat applied

explanation: Use of full carburetor heat at full throttle results in a loss of approximately 150 to 200 RPM.

question: What type of carburetor is fitted to the O-235-L2C, and where is fuel obtained for the manual primer?

options.text: A down-draft, pressure-injection carburetor; the primer draws fuel from the carburetor bowl
A side-draft carburetor with no primer system fitted
An up-draft, float-type, fixed jet carburetor; the primer draws fuel from the fuel strainer
An up-draft, float-type carburetor; the primer draws fuel directly from the fuel tanks

explanation: The engine has an up-draft, float-type, fixed jet carburetor; the manual primer draws fuel from the fuel strainer and injects it into the cylinder intake ports.

question: How is the muffler constructed to also provide carburetor heat and cabin heater air?

options.text: With an internal electric heating element
By routing exhaust gas directly into the cabin
By using engine coolant to warm the intake air
With a shroud around the outside forming a heating chamber

explanation: The muffler is constructed with a shroud around the outside which forms a heating chamber for carburetor heat and cabin heater air.

question: How does ram air for engine cooling reach the cylinders, and is there a manual cooling control?

options.text: It enters through cowling intakes and is directed by baffling; no manual control is provided
It is drawn through the oil cooler first, then a manual valve directs it to the cylinders
A pilot-operated cowl flap controls cooling airflow
Cooling air is supplied by an engine-driven fan

explanation: Ram air enters through two intake openings in the front of the cowling and is directed around the cylinders by baffling; no manual cooling system control is provided.

question: What temperature threshold makes installation of the winterization kit advisable?

options.text: Operations in temperatures consistently below 10°C (50°F)
Operations in temperatures consistently below -7°C (20°F)
Operations above 32°C (90°F)
The kit is required at all times regardless of temperature

explanation: The winterization kit should be installed for operations in temperatures consistently below -7°C (20°F).

question: During cold weather starting with preheat, to what RPM is the throttle adjusted for approximately one minute after the engine starts?

options.text: 600 to 800 RPM
800 to 1000 RPM

explanation: After starting with preheat, the throttle is adjusted for 1200 to 1500 RPM for approximately one minute, after which RPM can be lowered to 1000 or less.

question: When starting without preheat in cold weather, what additional priming is used compared to starting with preheat?

options.text: No priming is used at all without preheat
Half the normal priming is used
Ten additional strokes are required
Three additional strokes just prior to pulling the propeller through by hand

explanation: Starting without preheat follows the same procedure as with preheat, except the engine is primed an additional three strokes just prior to pulling the propeller through by hand.

question: When operating in temperatures below -18°C, why should partial carburetor heat be avoided?

options.text: Partial heat may raise carburetor air temperature into the 0° to 21°C range, where icing is critical
Partial heat causes the engine to run too cold
Partial heat drains the battery excessively
Partial heat is mechanically impossible below -18°C

explanation: Partial carburetor heat may increase carburetor air temperature into the 0° to 21°C range, where icing is critical under certain atmospheric conditions, so it should be avoided below -18°C.
